correctness.rationale: Expand each intensity into Fourier k-harmonics 0,±1; their orthogonality for N>=3 yields ||Jh||_dat²=4Σ(αu_j+βu_{j+1})²+2tΣ(u_j+u_{j+1})²+2tΣ(v_j-v_{j+1})². Fourier diagonalization gives amplitude eigenvalues 4−4t+12t cos(2πk/N) and phase eigenvalues 4t(1−cos(2πk/N)). The only obligatory null is global imaginary constant; the amplitude minimum and phase nonzero minimum give the two affine terms. Their unique intersection occurs at t_N*=1/(1+3c_N+2sin²(π/N)) ∈ (0,1/4], with equality 1/4 only N=3. Numerical independent real Jacobians N=3,4,5,6,9,12 matched all eigenvalues including multiplicities to machine precision; general proof is analytic.
